dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Hey Michael, can you teach me important words for gọi món in Vietnam? I want to order by myself without asking others for help.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Sure! The most basic term is "gọi món". When you enter a restaurant, you just need to say "cho tôi gọi món". What dish do you thích most in Vietnam?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Hmm, I thích pho, but every time I order I get confused with the word "ớt". You Vietnamese thích spicy food too much! I said "không ớt" but they still put chili in my dish.

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: Is that so? You need to clearly say "không ớt, không hành" if you don't like them. We Vietnamese think food without seasoning lacks soul. To gọi món well, you also need to know words like "tái" and "chín".

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: What is "tái"? I thought it meant "come back". Last time I said "tái" to the pho seller, she laughed at me. Your culture is so hard to understand!

dialogue.speaker: Michael
dialogue.text: "Tái" in food means rare meat, not fully cooked. If you want well-done meat, say "thịt chín". Hey, next weekend I could take you out to eat and show you how to gọi món properly? You won't be laughed at anymore.
